newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries firm after income, spending data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries firm after income, spending data.

text.p: U.S. Treasury opened narrowly mixed on Monday and firmed slightly after the government reported November personal income and spending data.
The government said U.S. personal income rose 0.5 percent in November, slightly below economists' average forecast of a 0.6 percent gain.

Personal spending, however, also rose 0.5 percent during the month, topping the average forecast in the Reuters poll of 0.3 percent. Spending for October was also revised up to a gain of 0.7 pct from the previously reported rise of 0.5 pct.
The only other data the market gets on Monday is the University of Michigan's final December reading on consumer sentiment, which economists anticipate will measure 99.0.

Trading is expected to be quiet in a week bisected by Christmas. The U.S. Treasury market will close early -- at 1400 EST/1900 GMT on Tuesday, Christmas eve, and will be shut for Christmas on Wednesday.
Treasuries traded quietly overnight and in early trade on Monday.
Many market participants are taking the week off for an extended Christmas holiday.

"It's very quiet," said Matthew Alexy. "Tokyo was closed overnight. Nothing happened in London. We have some numbers at 8:30 and at 10 o'clock. Everyone is heading out the door to go Christmas shopping."
Alexy said most likely, the market will trade in a range, maybe testing some of its technical boundaries, said Alexy.
Otherwise, the market faces a light week of data, with main event being Friday's release of November durable goods orders.

"I'd be surprised if the (March T-bond) went below 112-24 on the Board," said Alexy. "For the long bond yield, the span between 6.57 percent and 6.63 percent is probably the range we have today," he said.
In thin trade, however, there is room for a surprise.
"If some one comes in and tries to push it, prices could move more sharply," said Alexy. "That's a possibility, but I'd be a little surprised."
The 30-year Treasury bond was unchanged at 98-20/32, yielding 6.61 percent, in initial trades but rose to 98-25/32, up 5/32, yielding 6.59 percent, toward mid-morning.
